{"title":"Practical convex optimization for ML (intuition + recognition + implications)","content":"### Plan overview
You want high-level intuition (not theorem-proving) focused on ML: recognizing convex objectives (e.g., logistic regression), understanding what convexity guarantees, and using optimizers/solvers intelligently.

We’ll build this in parallel modules, then merge into a compact mental model + checklist + a short learning path with examples.

### What you’ll get at the end
- A geometric intuition for convex sets/functions and why they matter
- A practical “is this convex?” recognition checklist (composition rules + Hessian/2nd-derivative shortcuts)
- Logistic regression convexity explained (what’s convex in which variables)
- What convexity implies for gradient descent (global optimum, convergence behaviors, step size implications)
- Practical guidance for using existing solvers (GD/SGD, LBFGS, Newton, coordinate descent, CVX/CVXPY) and diagnosing issues

### Execution structure
- 4 independent content-building tasks (can be done in parallel)
